title: UL/NIST vents: four natural gas fires in a 6.1 x 4.3 x 2.4 m room with a door and two ceiling vents, the first interval of each (NIST at UL, 2012)
reference: Opert, K. (2012). Assessment of natural vertical ventilation for structural fire fighting. M.S. thesis, University of Maryland, as described in the FDS Validation Guide (NIST SP 1018-3), section UL/NIST Vent Experiments
notice: Measurements from NIST's Fire Research Division Experimental Database (github.com/firemodels/exp) and test conditions from NIST's FDS validation inputs (github.com/firemodels/fds), both carrying NIST's notice: NIST-developed works, not subject to copyright protection within the United States; acknowledge the National Institute of Standards and Technology as the source; modified works should note the date and nature of any change. Changed here (2026-11-11): reduced to the numbers compared by tools/calibration/validation-suite.mjs (thermocouple trees reduced by Janssens and Tran's method at each measured time; point readings within the compared windows; geometry and burner read from the FDS inputs).
heldOut: never used to fit any solver parameter (fire-calibration-plan-2026-11-11.md, section 12)

tests.ventilation: door open (0.9 m x 2.1 m), both ceiling vents shut (the first interval)

burner.ramp: FDS RAMP_Q 'burner ramp' x HRRPUA 1562.5 kW/m2 x 0.640 m2, to the first interval's end (1215 s)
burner.radiantSource: FDS's default for METHANE (0.2; the input gives none)

fuel.name: methane
fuel.source: natural gas as methane; soot yield from the FDS input's REAC (none given: 0); CO2 by the carbon balance
